item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-ca493c2f7b41acc6","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"CONEVAL published a first-edition August 2023 qualitative study examining access to the right to health for people without social security amid reforms to the General Health Law, INSABI, and federalization of state health services.","question_ids":["6B.1","6B.2","6B.5","6B.10","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Directly relevant to 2023 health-policy implementation and access; the supplied extract gives the study’s scope but not its substantive findings.","ruler_attribution":"The extract identifies reforms and service changes but does not attribute them individually to López Obrador.","limitations":["Only the publication page and study description are supplied; substantive findings, outcomes, budgets, and corrective actions are unavailable."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8c22d062b6c31f18","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"CONEVAL’s monitoring report, first edition January 2024, reviewed 16 Mexican federal priority programs operating in 2023 across education, health, rural development, and economic well-being, serving groups including older adults, people with disabilities, farmers, and students.","question_ids":["6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.10","8B.2","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Directly covers 2023 programs, although the extract provides only the report’s scope and not program-level results.","ruler_attribution":"The source describes federal programs of the Mexican administration but does not attribute individual design or implementation decisions to López Obrador.","limitations":["No program-specific indicators, execution data, distributional results, audits, or corrections appear in the supplied units."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b7b3af195568098a","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"IMCO reported that the 2023 federal budget provided only small real increases or a real cut for programs addressing violence against women, specialized shelters, and victim services, while the Maya Train allocation was 130 times the combined allocation of those programs. It also reported that the federal executive had eliminated Full-Time Schools and shifted extended-school-day responsibilities to La Escuela es Nuestra, which the Superior Audit Institution had found lacked control, supervision, and follow-up mechanisms in its 2021 spending.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.7","5B.8","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.8","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The budget and program decisions concern 2023; the cited audit finding concerns 2021 implementation and is used as a qualification on the successor arrangement.","ruler_attribution":"The article attributes the budget, school-program elimination, and successor-program choice to the federal executive under López Obrador.","limitations":["The article was published in November 2022 and relies partly on 2021 spending; it does not establish 2023 execution or later correction."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f0a49cbb71eb1304","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"The CNDH recognized recent efforts by civil society, federal authorities, legislators, and the Nueva Escuela Mexicana to advance Mexico’s implementation of the Marrakech Treaty and the reading rights of people with disabilities, but reported insufficient accessible works, incomplete public cataloging, inadequate technical knowledge among library personnel, and unresolved inclusion of disability groups beyond visual disability.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.8","6B.10","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The statement is dated September 30, 2023 and directly evaluates implementation during the period.","ruler_attribution":"The CNDH attributes broad efforts to federal authorities and legislators but does not isolate López Obrador’s personal decisions.","limitations":["The extract does not identify budgets, staffing levels, responsible agencies, or whether the identified deficiencies were corrected."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a08201bd9e7f65d0","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"CONEVAL’s first strategic health evaluation, published in September 2022, assessed Mexico’s capacity to guarantee the right to health amid changes to the General Health Law, pandemic effects, and the design and coherence of programs for people without social security.","question_ids":["6B.1","6B.2","6B.5","6B.6","6B.10","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Pre-2023 baseline relevant to inherited health-system conditions and policy continuity, not a direct 2023 outcome assessment.","ruler_attribution":"The extract concerns federal health policy during López Obrador’s administration but does not attribute specific findings or decisions to him.","limitations":["Only the evaluation’s scope is supplied; no diagnostic findings, outcome measures, or implemented corrections are available."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d83820f777bd180b","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"ARTICLE 19 recorded 272 attacks against journalists and media in Mexico during January–June 2023, including 68 intimidation or harassment cases, 61 cases of illegitimate use of public power, and 49 threats. It attributed 140 attacks—about half—to authorities, with state officials responsible for 23.5%, federal officials for 19.4%, and municipal officials for 8.4%; it also documented killings possibly linked to expression and a disappearance during the broader cited incidents.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.3","3B.4","3B.6","3B.8","3B.9","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","4B.10","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly covers the first half of 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes attacks to authorities at multiple levels and reports a federal share, but does not establish that López Obrador personally directed any specific attack.","limitations":["The extract reports documented attacks and recommendations, not final judicial findings, federal command responsibility, or the president’s response to each case."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c0bbe6a0262fedc3","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"UNICEF described Mexico’s education system as marked by deep inequities and severe foundational-learning deficits, and reported that a government-led Learning Camps initiative using Teaching at the Right Level, with UNICEF and partners, reached thousands of children with targeted literacy and numeracy instruction and produced measurable gains within weeks.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.10","8B.2","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The supplied extract does not date the intervention to 2023; it provides a relevant administration-era education implementation example and baseline context.","ruler_attribution":"UNICEF attributes the initiative to Mexico’s Ministry of Education, with UNICEF and partners; it does not name López Obrador personally.","limitations":["The extract does not provide exact dates, budget, geographic distribution, comparison group, or evidence of national-scale durability."]},{"source_id":"SRC-29edbc078fca6a98","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"In January 2023, López Obrador said that after Norma Piña became president of the Supreme Court, his administration observed more acts it considered illegal and unjust; he instructed that cases of public interest be taken to the FGR, Federal Judiciary Council, and Supreme Court while stating that the executive respected judicial decisions.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.4","4B.6","7B.1","7B.6","7B.7","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly dated to January 2023, with the article updated in March 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The statements and instruction are directly attributed to López Obrador.","limitations":["The source reports allegations and rhetoric, not verified illegality, institutional follow-through, or whether the referrals produced findings."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9a82e2ae372a5a8d","start_unit":27,"end_unit":29,"fact_summary":"Banco de México’s consumption-determinants table for its 2022 fourth-quarter report shows seasonally adjusted January 2023 real wage mass at 44.21, consumer confidence at 43.65, and remittances at 5.19 billion dollars, with the table documenting the underlying series and sources.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.7","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10","8B.7"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Provides one January 2023 observation and a pre-2023 historical series; it is an economic outcome/context source rather than a direct evaluation of presidential policy.","ruler_attribution":"The table is produced by Banco de México using ENOE/INEGI, consumer-confidence, and remittance data; it does not attribute outcomes to López Obrador.","limitations":["The supplied extract contains no counterfactual, policy attribution, distributional breakdown, or full-year 2023 result."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f82036a36c11e803","start_unit":1,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Mexico’s Juan Ramón de la Fuente was elected president of the Second Meeting of States Parties to the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons, held November 27–December 1, 2023; the UN described his professional background and senior public and international experience.","question_ids":["1B.4","1B.7","1B.10","8B.4","8B.5","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly covers a 2023 international disarmament meeting, but concerns Mexico’s representative and the meeting’s institutional leadership rather than a documented personal decision by López Obrador.","ruler_attribution":"The source identifies De la Fuente as Mexico’s Permanent Representative to the UN from 2019–2023 but does not attribute his election or conduct to López Obrador.","limitations":["No Mexican presidential statement, treaty decision, funding record, or implementation action is supplied."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-4d70964e77aaae1b"],"batch_limitations":["The supplied extracts are webpage summaries and selected article units, not complete underlying reports or datasets.","Several sources provide institutional or administration-level evidence without isolating López Obrador’s personal responsibility.","No evidence in the supplied documents materially addresses chapters 1B beyond general treaty-context evidence, or 2B beyond the absence of conflict-related material.","Facts are limited to what is explicitly stated in the supplied labeled units; no scores are assigned."]}
